questions.q: How does Google decide which businesses rank on Google Maps?
questions.a: Google ranks local results on three main factors: relevance, distance and prominence. Relevance is how well your business matches the search, distance is how close you are to the searcher, and prominence is how well-known and trusted you appear online. You can't change where searchers are, but you can make your listings complete and accurate.

questions.q: How do I improve my restaurant's ranking on Google Maps?
questions.a: Start by completing every field of your Google Business Profile, including categories, hours, photos, attributes and a description with local keywords. Then build a steady stream of fresh reviews and reply to them. Keeping your name, address and phone number consistent across directories also helps Google trust your listing.

questions.q: Do reviews affect Google Maps rankings?
questions.a: Yes, the quantity, quality and freshness of your reviews all feed into your Maps ranking. Recent reviews also matter to customers, who tend to trust them more than older ones. Asking right after a visit, sending a direct link by text or email and replying to every review keeps the stream going.

questions.q: What is NAP consistency and why does it matter?
questions.a: NAP stands for name, address and phone number, the core details of each listing. When these differ across Google, Yelp, Apple Maps and other directories, both Google and customers get confused. Consistent details, along with matching categories and website links, help your listings earn trust.

questions.q: How can a multi-location brand manage local SEO for every store?
questions.a: Centralize listing management in one platform so you aren't logging into dozens of dashboards. Give each location its own local signals, such as nearby landmarks and photos from that store, and track views, calls and direction requests per location. Momos's Listings Management suite automates these steps, syncing data across directories and flagging inconsistencies.
